Historical Jesus or Jesus Myth: The
Jesus
Puzzle

Did Christianity
begin
with an historical Jesus or a Jesus myth? Was the original Jesus a man
or a mythical savior god? Solving the Jesus Puzzle through the
Christian
and ancient-world record, from the Pauline epistles to the Gospels to
the
second century Christian apologists, from Philo to Josephus to Jewish
and
Hellenistic philosophy.

Christian faith evolved
from
a Jesus myth to an historical Jesus. New Testament scholarship needs to
uncover that original evolution and rewrite the history of Western
religion.

The results of your scholarship deserve the widest possible
dissemination,
and I hope against hope that your book will serve as a catalyst for
opening
some minds and putting truth in the spotlight. Long live rational
thought!"
(
Bill, Reader Feedback set 15
)

"An excellent site. Easily the best example of independent scholarship
on the Web." (

Early Christian Writings
 

Peter Kirby has created a very useful web site filled with information
on
all the Christian texts of the first two centuries. There is an entry
for each document which includes all the translations of that document
that are online, all of the scholarly online resources that are
available,
and titles of relevant books as well as commentary and quotes provided
by Kirby that detail the dating, provenance, and significance of the
work.

Early Christian
Writings

Kirby has also written an essay on the authenticity of the references
to Jesus in 
Josephus

and a survey of various contemporary 
theories
about the historical Jesus
. He also has a web site devoted to the 
Gospel of Thomas
, and has
developed a sister site for 
Early Jewish Writings
.

Finally, Kirby is editing a web site called 
"Did Jesus Exist?"
 for essays
on Christian origins, which welcomes contributions from various points
of view.

* * *
 

A Compelling Exercise in Radical Criticism
 

Despite all efforts of historical criticism during the past two
centuries,
the origins of Christianity remain hidden in deep darkness. Even modern
research has not been successful in throwing full light upon them.
According
to Radical Criticism, this is due to the fact that the decisive
presuppositions
of previous work on the history of early Christianity have never been
questioned
methodically. This is true especially for the supposed genuineness of
important
documents of early Christianity as, for example, the Ignatian letters,
1 Clement and all of Paul’s Epistles. Radical Criticism has shown that
their genuineness has by no means been firmly established. Nor can the
human Jesus of Nazareth as a figure of history be regarded as a
self-evident
basic assumption.  

Following the footsteps of the German critic Bruno Bauer and of the
Dutch Radical School (W.C. Van Manen, G.A. van den Bergh van Eysinga),
Radical Criticism tries to excavate the roots of early Christanity
without
any ecclesiastical or ideological bias. 

http://www.radikalkritik.de
